title: Subscale Booster Motor Test at Marshall Space Flight Center
description: The Subscale Booster Motor Test at Marshall Space Flight Center was the third in the series to evaluate the alternate materials for possible use in the nozzle and motor insulation and built upon prior tests at Marshall in 2022 and 2021. The subscale motor tests are an essential part of learning how a full-scale BOLE booster will perform during flight.

title: White Sands Test Facility (WSTF) Flammability Test Chamber Capabilities
description: The flammability test chamber is one of several chambers at White Sands Test Facility that can be used to test materials or components for flame propagation evaluation. Testing is conducted by providing an overwhelming ignition source to the material, and evaluating if the material will extinguish at a given oxygen concentration and pressure.

title: White Sands Test Facility (WSTF) Offgas Testing Capabilities
description: Offgas Testing at White Sands Test Facility identifies and quantifies the volatile offgassed products from materials and assembled articles that will be located within habitable regions of a spacecraft. Offgassing is the release of gaseous products from a material into an atmosphere that can accumulate in a closed-loop environment and potentially create a poisonous environment.

title: White Sands Test Facility (WSTF) Hypervelocity Impact Testing Capabilities
description: The White Sands Test Facility Remote Hypervelocity Test Laboratory is an access‐controlled hazardous test area capable of simulating Micrometeoroid and Orbital Debris impacts on spacecraft materials and components. The Hypervelocity Test Lab is capable of implementing test programs that propel projectiles at toxic or explosive materials and components such as batteries, aerospace fluids, and pressurized containers in a controlled laboratory environment.

title: White Sands Test Facility (WSTF) Mechanical Impact Testing Capabilities
description: The White Sands Test Facility is equipped with two mechanical impact test systems, an ambient and a pressurized test system. Mechanical impact testing is used to evaluate material ignition sensitivity in liquid and gaseous oxygen environments and to rank materials for best selection and design for liquid oxygen applications. Both these test systems can be customized to answer a specific ignition concern in these environments.
